messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Rolling SLO breach detected for /v1/generate-stream. 5m window p99 = 2.1s (>1.8s SLO). Auto-page -> oncall.

mike (oncall): ack — I'm taking the page. looking at grafana now. any customer reports? :eyes:  

deepa (eng-sre): seeing p95 jump 450ms -> 750ms, p99 2.1s. error rate up ~0.7%. long streaming sessions show stalls at token boundaries (stalls ~800-1300ms).

jordan (support): CS reported latency from acme-inc for large convo flows, several sessions timed out. opening incident ticket for affected customers.

anne (eng-runtime): quick look at runtime metrics: a single GPU node gpu-node-az3-12 has repeated ECC correctable spikes and thermal throttle events correlated with stall timestamps. KV cache misses + stall traces point to hardware hiccups, not model CPU. recommend draining that node and routing traffic away ASAP.

kyle (infra): starting drain of gpu-node-az3-12 now. will remove from pool and trigger re-route to pool-B. ETA for drain ~60s.

mike (oncall): ok, please also spin up a fallback route: shift 40% of streaming traffic to redwood-small-quant (lower perf but stable) and enable canary fallback for remaining traffic if we see additional p99 spikes.

anne (eng-runtime): applying route change:
```
# deploy commands
redwood route update --route /v1/generate-stream --model redwood-small-quant --percent 40 --mode canary
infra@infra: drain gpu-node-az3-12 --reason "thermal/ECC p99 stalls"
```

# logs snippet (sensitive timings scrubbed):
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] gpu-node-az3-12: ECC_CORRECTABLE count=42 window=5m
[2026-03-15T12:03:25Z] gpu-node-az3-12: THERMAL_THROTTLE GPU0 temp=89C -> throttle_start
[2026-03-15T12:03:30Z] runtime: STREAMING_STALL id=abc123 duration=1200ms cause=kv_miss
```

deepa (eng-sre): confirming: after drain started p99 dropped to ~1.4s in last minute; p95 back to ~480ms. still monitoring for tail flares.

jordan (support): telling CS: active mitigation in progress (draining degraded node + fallback model). ETA for normal latencies ~5-10m. will update customers.

mike (oncall): question for infra/runtime: do we have a permanent RMA candidate for gpu-node-az3-12? looks flaky.

kyle (infra): yes, we've flagged it for HW replacement — observed correctable ECC counts exceed threshold. we'll RMA after the drain completes.

anne (eng-runtime): additional note: streaming stalls appear when KV cache hits drop below baseline (likely due to node reboot/eviction). adding short-term mitigation: increase prefix cache replication factor for pool-B to reduce miss amplification.

deepa (eng-sre): handover notes for next oncall: root cause likely combination of intermittent ECC events triggering thermal throttle which causes degraded throughput and KV cache churn -> streaming stalls -> p99 tail. mitigations applied: drained node, shifted 40% traffic to quantized fallback, increased cache replication, monitoring alert thresholds tightened for ECC count and thermal events.

mike (oncall): handing off in 30m to deepa. leaving runbook snippets here. please escalate to eng-runtime + infra if ECC count continues rising or if p99 > 1.8s again. :thumbsup:

anne (eng-runtime): runbook snippet: 
- Check node: `kubectl get pods -l node=gpu-node-az3-12`
- Collect dmesg + nvidia-smi logs
- If ECC_CORRECTABLE > 10 in 5m -> drain + RMA
- If THERMAL_THROTTLE events correlate with stalls -> schedule urgent HW swap

jordan (support): CS update posted to ticket, awaiting customer ack. marking affected customers list + mitigations.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (p99 back under SLO threshold). Auto-close timer set to 30m unless re-opened.

deepa (eng-sre): will pick up after mike leaves. adding postmortem draft pointer to /confluence/incidents/2360123456-postmortem (will fill details).

mike (oncall): thanks team. leaving the channel — deepa, you're owner. mike out. :wave:
